newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call inactive, gilt yields move southwards.
newsitem.headline: Indian call inactive, gilt yields move southwards.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed at 0.10-0.25 percent in a dull day's trade on a reporting Friday, against the opening levels of 0.25-0.50 percent, a dealer said.
"Very few deals have been reported today," a dealer with a state-run bank said.
The three-day money opened at 3.00-3.50 percent, but slipped to close at 2.00-2.50 percent, he said.
The market expects call rates to open below 5.0 percent on Saturday, dealers said.

Securities witnessed some buying interest in the morning and afternoon session, with sentiment depressed towards the close, a dealer said. "We will wait and watch the reaction of 14-day treasury bills on Saturday," he said.
The volume on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) rose to 6.0 billion rupees from the previous 5.28 billion, an NSE dealer said.
The 12.14 percent government stock 2000 rose to 100.64 rupees from its previous close of 100.50 rupees, and the 12.69 percent 2002 stock to 101.11 rupees from 100.95 rupees, a dealer said.
The yield on treasury bills maturing in April 1998 fell to 8.95 percent, against its previous 9.05 percent, he said.
The certificate of deposit of Indo-Gulf Fertiliser Ltd. maturing in August dealt at 9.40 percent, he added.
